title: Wake up!
takeaway: The sun has risen. Times have changed. Wake up and get to work.
scene: An untitled call to action at the top of page 99. It sounds like a rousing chant: 'Jaago!', which means 'Wake up!'

original: جوانو جاگو جاگو قوم دے پاسبانو جاگو
گوڑی نیند وچ ستے نوجوانو جاگو
transliteration: Javaano jaago, jaago, qaum de paasbaano jaago
Goorhi neend vich sutte naujavaano jaago
translation: Young people, wake up, wake up! Guardians of the nation, wake up!
Young ones sunk in deep sleep, wake up!
couplets.story: He shouts to the young people of the country: wake up! You're meant to be the country's guardians, but you're fast asleep.

original: جاگو جاگو میرے مزدور کسانو جاگو
چڑھے ہوئے سورج دی چمک نوں دیکھو
transliteration: Jaago jaago mere mazdoor kisaano jaago
Charhe hoe sooraj di chamak nu dekho
translation: Wake up, wake up, my workers and farmers, wake up!
Look at the shining of the risen sun.
couplets.story: Wake up, workers and farmers! The sun is already high in the sky.

original: آج دے بدلے موسم نوں احمدؔ پچھانو جاگو
transliteration: Ajj de badle mausam nu Ahmad pachhaano, jaago
translation: Ahmad says: recognise how the times have changed today, and wake up!
couplets.story: Times have changed. Notice it, and wake up!

why: Short, loud and energetic. It's easy to imagine it being chanted.
prompt: What's something you've been 'asleep' about that you want to wake up to?
notes: Untitled five-line verse at the top of page 99; it may continue a poem from page 98.
